_comment: What measurement gate 1 -- the capability gate -- records.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. performance-probe.schema.json requires
input_to_present_p50/p95/p99, missed_vsync_ratio and gpu_bytes on every
record. Gate 1 is defined as the gate that runs with NO RENDERER AND NO
VALIDATOR, so it cannot produce a single one of them. The first gate in the
measurement order therefore had no way to write down its result, and the
only shapes available were to invent numbers for fields that were not
measured, or to keep the answers in prose. Both are how a capability
becomes an assumption again.
The measurement order in the plan is itself a conclusion: gate 1 cuts the
candidate set every later gate draws from. A candidate that no device
supports must be removed before it is benchmarked, not after, because a
benchmark of an unavailable arm is a benchmark of the fallback that ran
instead.
SO THE RULE HERE IS DIFFERENT FROM THE PERFORMANCE SCHEMA'S. There, a
missing field rejects the run because a sample nobody can characterise
cannot be averaged. Here, an UNANSWERED capability is a legitimate result
-- some answers need an entitlement, a region, or an OS this device is not
-- but it must be recorded as `unsupported` or `not_probed` with evidence,
never omitted. An absent key and a false answer are the same thing to a
reader, and they are not the same thing to a decision.
Enforced by tools/apple-probe-decision/admit.py.
simulator_counts_as_evidence is false here for a narrower reason than in
the performance schema. The simulator runs the host's JavaScriptCore on
the host's CPU, so it answers 'is JIT on' with the host's answer, which
is yes on every Mac and tells you nothing about an iPhone in Lockdown
Mode. Some answers here -- whether a JS API is exposed at all -- would
in fact be the same, and admitting the schema-shaped half while
rejecting the device-shaped half is exactly the split nobody maintains
correctly. One rule, applied to the record.
_required_os_minors_comment: A21/A23/A24 are all version-sensitive, and 15.2 is the SharedArrayBuffer
boundary the coverage arithmetic turns on. A capability admitted from
one OS is a capability admitted for one OS.

_origin_comment: ONE RECORD PER ORIGIN, not one per device. Half the questions below are
answered by the origin and not by the device: whether the page is a
secure context, whether it is cross-origin isolated, and therefore
whether SharedArrayBuffer constructs at all. A single record per device
would have to hold two answers under one key, and the way that resolves
in practice is that whichever origin ran last wins silently.
The origin-independent answers -- JIT, Worker rAF -- are repeated in
both records. Repetition is the cheap half of this trade; a reader
comparing them across origins for a device is entitled to expect them to
agree, and a disagreement is a finding rather than a bookkeeping error.
_lockdown_comment: A24. Lockdown Mode disables JIT for web content unless the app is
explicitly excluded, so 'WebContent has JIT' is a device state and not
an admission invariant. `unknown` is honest and is not the same as
`off`: iOS exposes no public query for it, so a probe that cannot infer
it from the JIT answer must say so rather than assume the common case.

_comment: The closed set of questions gate 1 asks about one origin on one device.
Each settles a numbered assumption in the plan's ledger, and each names
the assumption so a reader can find out what turns on the answer.
POLARITY IS FIXED: `available` always means the architecture MAY use
this. That is why the local-network question is phrased as the absence
of a prompt rather than its presence -- a set of capabilities where
`available` means good for nine entries and bad for the tenth is a set
whose admission rule has to special-case one of them, and the
special case is what gets lost.
Closed on purpose, for the same reason the performance enums are: a
capability name the decision cannot recognise is a probe measuring
something nothing consumes, and accepting it silently reports coverage
that does not exist.
capabilities.jit_enabled: A24. Whether WebContent actually got JIT, probed rather than inferred. The whole architecture rests on this and Lockdown Mode can turn it off. Origin-independent; recorded in both records so a disagreement is visible.
capabilities.secure_context: A5/A6/A23. Whether this origin is a secure context. For the custom scheme this is A23, whose claim that it needs private API rests on a specification that in fact lets a user agent designate trustworthy schemes.
capabilities.cross_origin_isolated: A7/A23. Whether this origin reports crossOriginIsolated === true with COOP and COEP actually served.
capabilities.shared_array_buffer: A15. Whether SharedArrayBuffer constructs in a Worker at this origin. Downstream of cross_origin_isolated, and recorded separately because the two have been observed to disagree.
capabilities.atomics_wait: A21. Whether Atomics.wait blocks and wakes in a Worker, measured by elapsed time and not by the function existing.
capabilities.sync_xhr_binary: A21. Whether a synchronous XMLHttpRequest in a Worker returns a binary body. The second public blocking primitive, and the one that decides whether Window is excluded on capability grounds at all.
capabilities.websocket_in_worker: A22. Whether WebSocket is constructible and connectable from a Worker, which is what makes the Window relay a consequence of blocking rather than an API requirement.
capabilities.worker_raf: A18. Whether DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope.requestAnimationFrame exists. The design does not depend on it; the probe exists so the feature detection has a measured answer in both directions.
capabilities.request_body_delivery: A5. Whether a POST body reaches the other side of this origin's transport intact. For the custom scheme that is the WKURLSchemeHandler, and WebKit 191362 is RESOLVED FIXED, so this measures shipping behaviour rather than restating a bug report.
capabilities.no_local_network_prompt: A6/G0.3. Whether this origin works WITHOUT the local-network permission alert. `unavailable` means the alert appeared, which is a review and onboarding problem and not only a latency one. `unsupported` for an origin that opens no socket.

_comment: One capability's answer. `evidence` is required on every one, including
the yeses: 'true' with no evidence is indistinguishable from a probe
that returned a default, and this project has already recorded a case
where a lane reported success while checking nothing.
_state_comment: `unavailable` means the probe ran and the answer was no.
`unsupported` means this OS or device cannot be asked -- the API is not
present to fail. `not_probed` means nobody asked, which is the one that
must never be quietly read as no.
